title: Vast AI Workflow: How to Rent a GPU (2026 Guide)
summary: A Vast AI workflow consists of six steps: search offers, rent an instance, connect, run the job, copy the output, and destroy the instance.
body_markdown:
## Automating Vast AI Jobs with Activepieces


**Destroying the instance is the step people forget** on the tenth run, not the first.


Describe that cleanup in the built-in chat of Activepieces, whose core is MIT-licensed, and it publishes a live flow in your account, the same flow a builder would have assembled by hand.


It's governed like any flow someone built manually, with RBAC, audit logs and run traces, so nobody needs hiring to write it.


Nothing here is a one-click integration: none of the 750 integrations counted in the open source monorepo is a dedicated Vast.ai connector.


What Activepieces does have is a generic HTTP step, and Vast.ai exposes a REST API, so the same calls you made by hand in the console can run as a flow.


If you rent a GPU once a quarter, skip it. If you launch the same job every week, the flow replaces the part of the checklist that depends on your memory.


It always runs in one shape: a trigger starts it, an HTTP step calls the Vast.ai API, and the result branches.


It traces that path from the trigger on the left to the two outcomes on the right, an alert message and the destruction of an idle instance.


### Destroy idle instances on a schedule


Use a schedule trigger, such as every evening, and add an HTTP step that asks the Vast.ai API for your current instances. Authenticate it with your API key stored as a connection rather than pasted into the step.


A branch step then checks each instance against the rule you chose, for example that it has no job attached, and a second HTTP step sends the destroy request for those that match.


When an instance is destroyed that shouldn't have been, you open the run, read the exact response the list call returned, and see which condition matched.


Every run leaves a trace of each step's input and output. That's a record you can debug, which the console's billing page is not.


Flows are unlimited on every plan, including free, so this destroy flow and the alert flow below can sit side by side without costing you a plan upgrade.


### Alert when an instance runs too long


Nothing is destroyed in this one. It uses the same list call, compares how long each instance has been running with a limit you set, and sends a message to email or a chat channel when one exceeds it.


Use this where a long run may be legitimate, such as training that's meant to take days, and deletion would throw away work.


The alert tells a person to decide, and the run trace shows what the API reported when the message fired.


Rent one cheap on-demand instance, run the flow's destroy step against it, and open the run trace to confirm the instance is gone from your account. Do this before you trust the flow with anything expensive.
